snapshot.summary: Seat 1 opened with Exchange (Ambassador) and later Tax (Duke) and Assassinate (Assassin). Seat 2 also opened Exchange, then Tax and Assassinate claims. Seat 3 opened Tax (Duke) twice. Rounds 1-6 were uncontested taxes/exchanges. Turning point: Round 7 Seat 1 assassinated Seat 3 (Captain revealed), and Round 8 Seat 2 assassinated Seat 3 again eliminating Seat 3. Round 11 Seat 1's assassinate on Seat 2 was blocked by Seat 2 as Contessa and accepted. Final: Round 14 Seat 2 assassinated Seat 1, Seat 1 challenged, Seat 2 proved Assassin, Seat 1 lost its last cards (Ambassador, Assassin) and was eliminated. Seat 2 won as last player with hidden cards at Round 14 in phase end, with 5 coins and 2 hidden vs 0.

=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

[user]
=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.

=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Coup (XColos) ===

Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.

records.system:
You are the referee of a turn-based game. You are not a player and you never speak to one. You are shown the complete state of the table, including information the players cannot see, and asked to produce one thing.

Answer only from the state you are given. Do not guess at anything not shown, do not reason about what a player is likely to do next, and do not soften a clear answer. If the state does not settle the question, say so by answering false or by returning nothing usable, rather than inventing an answer.

THE GAME
Each player holds two hidden role cards from a 15-card deck (3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador, Contessa) and has coins. Seat 1 starts with 1 coin and every other seat with 2. Revealed cards are face up, public and permanent.

On your turn choose one action: Income (+1; no challenge or block); Foreign Aid (+2; no challenge; any player may block as Duke); Coup (pay 7; the target loses 1 influence; no challenge or block; compulsory with 10 or more coins); Tax (claims Duke, +3); Assassinate (claims Assassin, pay 3, the target loses 1 influence; the target may block as Contessa); Steal (claims Captain, take 2 coins from the target or all they have if fewer; the target may block as Captain or Ambassador); Exchange (claims Ambassador, draw a card then return one hidden card). Costs are never refunded.

Everyone else answers at the same moment: pass, challenge (only if a role is claimed), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger, and the first blocker, in seat order after the active player count. A challenged player who holds the role reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a card; the challenger loses 1 influence. Otherwise the challenged player loses 1 influence and the action fails. A block is then open to challenge by everyone but the blocker in the same way; if the block stands the action has no effect, if it fails the action goes ahead.

A player who loses one of two cards chooses which to reveal; a player who loses all hidden cards is out and their coins vanish. The last player with a hidden card wins. After 40 turns the player with the most hidden cards wins, ties go to the most coins, and a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free discussion: claims, challenges and blocks are the only communication.
